title: Ground ambulance service: historical standards, response compliance and hospital offloads
summary: The same audit documents compensation and service performance, but does not establish that compensation changes caused service results. Hospital offload measures and ambulance-provider response standards have different responsibilities and populations.

source.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Nova Scotia
source.title: Ground Ambulance Services: Department of Health and Wellness and Emergency Medical Care Inc.

institutionalLink.basis: Same original report and expressly named Department of Health and Wellness / Emergency Medical Care Inc. institutional contract context

responseDefinition.summary: Elapsed time from call taken to ambulance arrival on scene; priority and contract community category determine the threshold. Emergency uses lights/sirens; urgent does not.
responseDefinition.exemptions: Source permits exclusions for circumstances beyond provider control, including severe weather, disasters, specified technology failures and peak capacity.
responseDefinition.monitoringLimit: Report says departmental contractual-response monitoring stopped in August 2022. These July results are historical, not current compliance.

responseResults.measure: Contractual on-time response compliance, not mean or percentile minutes
responseResults.sourceStage: Department calculation reproduced in auditor report; graph explicitly labelled unaudited
responseResults.denominator: Eligible responses after exemptions; exact count and raw exemptions unavailable in this slice

offloadStandard.wordingStrength: strive to meet a target, as described in the auditor report; not a newly inferred absolute legal deadline
offloadStandard.responsibility: Hospital transfer of care is not an EMCI performance standard. The performance table includes IWK separately; this does not establish applicability of the Nova Scotia Health directive to IWK.

offloadDefinition.summary: Interval from ambulance arrival at emergency department to recorded transfer of care to the hospital team. Arrival uses GPS; transfer time is manually recorded.
exclusions: Source excludes offload intervals shorter than two minutes and longer than twelve hours.
Missing transfer-of-care times and inconsistent manual recording reduce source confidence; these are not independently repaired.
offloadDefinition.excludedCountsLimit: Report-wide quality review spans April 2017–December 2022; those counts cannot serve as the denominator adjustment for this 2022 hospital table.

limitations: Historical 2022 measures, not current service performance or clinical patient outcomes.
Response compliance percentages are not average response minutes. Community targets are 80%; consolidated emergency/urgent target is 90%. Do not substitute one for the other.
July response data are reproduced departmental calculations labelled unaudited; raw eligible call and exemption counts are not available here.
The 30-minute hospital offload target is a different measure and institutional responsibility, not the provider response threshold or a legal liability conclusion.
The offload table covers twelve tertiary/regional hospitals, not all hospitals or all emergency responses. IWK population is age-limited.
Whole percentages are rounded. Do not infer exact successful-offload counts or recompute the source aggregate by taking an unweighted mean.
The hospital total and Average are overlapping aggregate rows, not additional hospitals. Dash cells remain null.
Compensation uses fiscal-year labels while these results use calendar periods; no per-dollar outcome ratio, causal inference, annual trend or matched-period financial comparison is established.
The original contract and directives are not independently acquired; source-attributed descriptions do not establish present legal obligations.
nextEvidenceNeeded: Lawfully available original contract schedules and directives with effective dates.
Period-matched departmental response calculations and exemption review records.
Hospital offload denominator/exclusion documentation and later verified performance releases.
A defensible causal evaluation would require broader costs, staffing, hospital capacity and other confounders, not just compensation totals.
rightsScope: Numerical institutional facts, source identifiers and concise independently written context only; no patient information, report facsimile, logos or extended narrative. No blanket source-content reproduction licence.
